measurements.note: Descriptive run-level distributions only. No startup speedup, physical-memory reduction or production/hardware performance claim.

limitations: Matching visible editor and normalized profiles do not establish background feature parity; the Rust build is a partial migration.
One Linux software-rendered Xvfb host, with background services present and load recorded; workers/builds/other goal GUI tests were paused.
Application/XDG caches were fresh; OS page cache was uncontrolled/warmed, with seeded alternating paired order.
PSS is the summed proportional resident share of every observed living app process; it is not unique physical memory and cannot attest unseen escaped helpers.
RSS sums count shared pages repeatedly and are reported separately.
CPU uses sampled observed-process own counters and remains a lower bound; exited/unseen short-lived helpers can be missed. No delegated cgroup was available.
Launch/control paths differ; no comparable startup, frame timing, hardware, sustained media or full-feature application claim.
Rust had lower observed PSS and higher observed CPU in this workload; no overall speedup or significance claim.
